# **Section 14 --- External Research Results (Q216--Q225)**

*Evidence gathered from external sources to inform architectural
decisions. Each entry includes references and key takeaways.*

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Q216**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          **Discord gateway/event coverage matrix for target interaction types.**
  **Answer:**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
  Research findings: Discord Gateway v10 (used by discord.py 2.x) exposes three privileged intents --- GUILD_MEMBERS (member join/leave/update), GUILD_PRESENCES (online status/activity), and MESSAGE_CONTENT (message body, attachments, embeds). All other intents (messages, reactions, voice states, threads, forum events, moderation) are standard and require no approval. Poll events (POLL_VOTE_ADD / POLL_VOTE_REMOVE) are available as of API v10. Gift interactions are NOT exposed to third-party bots. Reaction removes lack member info (Discord limitation). Without MessageContent intent: message content, attachments, and embeds fields return empty; timestamps and author ID still arrive.   
  **Confidence: High**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              **Source: ***Discord Gateway documentation; discord.py 2.x intent primer; Discord MessageContent FAQ; GitHub Gateway Intents Explainer (advaith1)*
  **Notes / Follow-up: **The critical gap is MessageContent --- design all reward predicates to function without content if the intent is not approved.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Q217**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      **Best practices for event-envelope schema versioning in Postgres JSONB systems.**
  **Answer:**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  Research findings: The consensus approach from multiple sources (Medium/Kokhan 2024, SoftwareMill) is: embed a version integer directly in each row (not just in JSONB), use additive-only schema evolution (never remove fields, never change semantics of existing fields), write version-specific upcasting functions in application code rather than migrating historical data, and use PostgreSQL\'s JSONB + GIN indexing for querying version-specific payload structures. Event store table design from SoftwareMill: (id SERIAL, stream_id BIGINT, version BIGINT, data JSONB, UNIQUE(stream_id, version)) with BIGSERIAL for ordering, since timestamps are unreliable (NTP drift, clock skew). For envelope schema, hybrid approach --- typed columns for query-critical fields, JSONB for event-specific payload --- is the recommended pattern.   
  **Confidence: High**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          **Source: ***SoftwareMill: \'Implementing event sourcing using a relational database\'; Medium/Kokhan: \'JSONB in PostgreSQL with EF Core Part 2\'; PostgreSQL official JSONB documentation*
  **Notes / Follow-up: **Key insight: use BIGSERIAL not timestamps for ordering --- sequence gaps are acceptable, clock skew is not.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Q218**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           **Rule engine patterns for deterministic evaluation + explainability.**
  **Answer:**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
  Research findings: Fowler\'s RulesEngine bliki establishes that the core risk of rule engines is chaining --- where one rule\'s action affects another\'s condition --- creating opaque behavior. Avoid chaining at v1. The Rete algorithm is the standard for efficient multi-rule matching but is overkill for sub-100-rule sets; simple linear scan with short-circuit evaluation is faster and more debuggable at this scale. Key determinism requirements from multiple sources: (1) fixed evaluation order (priority number), (2) stateless condition checks (no external calls during evaluation), (3) full trace logging of every condition evaluated and its result. The rule-engine PyPI package provides a typed expression language with custom grammar for matching Python objects --- viable as a foundation. YAML-stored rules with a Python evaluation layer is a proven pattern (Medium/van der Laan 2025) for maintainability.   
  **Confidence: High**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               **Source: ***Fowler: martinfowler.com/bliki/RulesEngine.html; datathrillz.com: \'Considerations for building a rules engine in Python\'; Nected: \'Rules Engine Design Patterns\'; Medium: \'The Python Rule Engine\' (van der Laan 2025); PyPI rule-engine package*
  **Notes / Follow-up: **Store rules as database records (not YAML files) so they can be versioned, snapshotted, and rolled back through the API.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Q219**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  **Anti-gaming heuristics for community systems (forum/reply/reaction abuse).**
  **Answer:**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
  Research findings: Community-specific anti-gaming draws from both game industry (Riot Games/League of Legends Tribunal, CS:GO cooldown system, Dota 2 behavior score) and platform design. Core proven heuristics: (1) per-user per-type rate limits / daily caps --- the most fundamental control; (2) velocity anomaly detection --- flag users who trigger the same reward event type N times in M minutes at rate far above guild average; (3) mutual interaction filtering --- remove reciprocal rewards when user A and user B consistently react to each other at abnormal rates; (4) minimum quality threshold --- reward only if the event meets a minimum content signal (e.g., message length \> 10 chars, forum reply is not just an emoji); (5) account age gates --- new accounts below 7 days guild tenure cannot earn above a low daily cap; (6) cooldown reset on moderation action --- if a user is warned/banned, review their recent earnings. Riot\'s key insight: toxic/gaming behavior comes from regular people in the wrong conditions, not just bad actors --- design for the majority first.   
  **Confidence: High**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      **Source: ***MIT Technology Review: \'A Video-Game Algorithm to Solve Online Abuse\'; Steam/Valve CS:GO cooldown guide; ARGOS Identity: \'Game Industry: Examining Game Abuse\'; Medium: \'How Scalable Systems Handle Abuse: Rate Limiting\'*
  **Notes / Follow-up: **Implement the five core heuristics as the always-on baseline (see Q8). Velocity anomaly detection can be a later add --- flag for human review rather than auto-penalize.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Q220**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          **Replayable projection architectures (event sourcing style) in Python/Postgres stacks.**
  **Answer:**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
  Research findings: SoftwareMill\'s event sourcing guide and the Medium/Hede PostgreSQL event sourcing article are the canonical references for this stack. Core pattern: events table (id, stream_id/guild_id, version, data JSONB, inserted_at) is immutable; projections are derived views rebuilt by replaying events through projection functions. In Python/PostgreSQL, projections can be maintained via: (1) application-level replay workers that query events in order and update projection tables, (2) PostgreSQL triggers on the events table that call projection functions (faster but couples logic to DB), or (3) scheduled reconciliation jobs. For Synapse, approach (1) is recommended --- an async Python worker that processes event rows in batches, ordered by (guild_id, occurred_at, id). Replay from scratch should be the recovery path for corrupted projections, not an edge case.   
  **Confidence: High**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              **Source: ***SoftwareMill: \'Implementing event sourcing using a relational database\'; Medium/Hede: \'Event Sourcing with PostgreSQL\'; Fowler: CQRS pattern documentation*
  **Notes / Follow-up: **Design the projection worker to be idempotent --- it must be safe to run twice against the same event range without double-counting.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Q221**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        **Partitioning + retention strategies for append-only telemetry tables in Postgres 16.**
  **Answer:**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  Research findings: The consensus across PostgreSQL official docs, Stormatics, Data Egret, blog.sequinstream.com, and multiple pg_partman guides is: use RANGE partitioning on a timestamp column (occurred_at or ingested_at), partition by month for telemetry at this scale, use pg_partman + pg_cron for automated partition creation and retention enforcement. Key technical details: set infinite_time_partitions = true in pg_partman config; pre-create 3 future monthly partitions (p_premake := 3); set retention to your chosen window (e.g., \'12 months\'); use retention_keep_table = true to detach-but-not-drop for archival, or false to drop and free disk. Dropping a partition is an instant metadata operation --- far superior to DELETE queries on large tables. For JSONB compression in large payload columns: PostgreSQL 14+ supports LZ4 compression (faster than default pglz) --- set per-column with ALTER TABLE \... ALTER COLUMN payload SET COMPRESSION lz4.   
  **Confidence: High**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            **Source: ***PostgreSQL official partitioning docs; Stormatics: \'Improving PostgreSQL Performance with Partitioning\'; Data Egret: \'Data archiving and retention in PostgreSQL\'; blog.sequinstream.com: \'Time-based retention strategies in Postgres\'; AWS RDS pg_partman guide; jamauriceholt.com: \'PostgreSQL Partitioning Best Practices\'*
  **Notes / Follow-up: **Run EXPLAIN on your most common projection queries to verify partition pruning is working (look for \'Partitions selected: N of M\' in the plan).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Q222**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               **Practical eventual-consistency UX patterns (freshness indicators, user trust).**
  **Answer:**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            
  Research findings: The core problem eventual consistency creates for UX is user confusion when they take an action and the UI does not immediately reflect it. Proven patterns: (1) Optimistic UI --- immediately show the user the expected result of their action and reconcile when the projection updates; (2) Explicit freshness indicators --- show \'Last updated: 2 minutes ago\' timestamps on stale data rather than hiding lag; (3) Stale-while-revalidate --- show cached data instantly, refetch in the background, and update without a jarring full-page refresh; (4) Skeleton loading states --- show the page structure immediately with animated placeholders while data loads; (5) Notification of lag --- \'Your recent activity may take a few minutes to appear\' is honest and manages expectations better than false precision. Research consistently shows users prefer honesty about data freshness over being misled by seemingly-instant but potentially wrong counters.   
  **Confidence: High**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   **Source: ***Engineering blog patterns on eventual consistency UX; SvelteKit data loading patterns; general UI/UX research on data freshness*
  **Notes / Follow-up: **In the Svelte dashboard, implement the \'stale-while-revalidate\' pattern using SvelteKit load functions with built-in cache control headers.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Q223**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               **Migration playbooks for moving from hardcoded logic to rules DSL.**
  **Answer:**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            
  Research findings: No single canonical source exists, but the pattern is well-understood from platform engineering experience. The migration playbook has five standard phases: (1) Inventory --- document every hardcoded condition and its output as a natural-language specification; (2) Translate --- express each hardcoded rule as a named rule in the new DSL and validate that the DSL is expressive enough; (3) Shadow --- run new DSL evaluator in parallel with old hardcoded logic, comparing outputs; (4) Parity check --- flag any event where outputs diverge and investigate; (5) Cut over --- disable old logic, monitor for divergence, maintain rollback path for 2 weeks. The key risk is undocumented edge cases in the old hardcoded logic that the new DSL does not model --- the shadow phase is designed to surface these.   
  **Confidence: High**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   **Source: ***Platform engineering migration patterns; event sourcing migration guides; practical experience distillation*
  **Notes / Follow-up: **Document every divergence found during the shadow phase --- they are either bugs in the new system or unknown features of the old one.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Q224**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       **Auditable rule lifecycle design (draft/publish/version/rollback).**
  **Answer:**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
  Research findings: The GitOps model applied to rule management is the established pattern. Core elements: (1) Every rule change produces an immutable version record with: rule_id, version_number, changed_by, changed_at, change_type (CREATED/UPDATED/PUBLISHED/ARCHIVED/ROLLED_BACK), full_definition (JSONB snapshot); (2) The \'active\' ruleset is a pointer to a versioned snapshot, not the live rule definitions --- changing this pointer is the publish/rollback operation; (3) Rollback = update the active pointer to a prior snapshot version, logged as a ROLLED_BACK event; (4) Draft rules exist outside the versioned snapshot system until published; (5) The audit log for rule changes must be immutable (no deletes, no updates) and retained indefinitely (separate from the event retention policy). This architecture supports point-in-time restore, compliance audits, and admin accountability.   
  **Confidence: High**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           **Source: ***GitOps pattern literature; Nected: \'Rules Engine Design Patterns\'; rule lifecycle management research; audit trail design principles*
  **Notes / Follow-up: **The active_ruleset_version pointer table is the most critical single-row table in the system --- protect it with careful transaction design.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Q225**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     **Data minimization/privacy patterns for community telemetry platforms.**
  **Answer:**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
  Research findings: GDPR Article 5(1)(c) data minimisation principle --- collect only data that is adequate, relevant, and limited to what is necessary --- is the foundational requirement. Proven patterns for community telemetry: (1) Metadata-only capture --- store structural features (message length, has_attachment) not message content; (2) Pseudonymization --- store Discord snowflake IDs as opaque integers rather than usernames; usernames change over time and are more personally identifiable; (3) Retention-at-ingest --- define retention limits before storing data, not after; (4) Right to erasure via anonymization --- replace actor_id with a null sentinel rather than deleting rows (preserves aggregate integrity while removing PII); (5) Data classification register --- document the sensitivity level of every stored field before implementation; (6) Access minimization --- raw telemetry accessible only to system operators, admins see only their guild\'s aggregates, end users see only their own summaries. Community-specific consideration: treat Discord user IDs as PII-equivalent even though they are pseudonymous --- they can be re-identified via Discord\'s public API if the account still exists.   
  **Confidence: High**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         **Source: ***GDPR Art. 5(1)(c); GDPR Art. 17 (erasure); ICO data minimisation guidance; privacy by design framework; Discord Developer Policy data requirements*
  **Notes / Follow-up: **Privacy design decisions made at the start are cheap to implement; privacy retrofits after launch are expensive and often incomplete.
